bull_bear.body:
- Brand trust and credibility - positioned as one of India's most trusted media networks, with a business model built on the principle that 'credibility creates value'
- Audience scale across digital platforms - 45 million lifetime YouTube subscribers across all NDTV Group channels, 102 million combined followers across social platforms and 40 billion video views across online platforms
- Diversified portfolio spanning news, lifestyle and digital formats, including English, Hindi, business and regional channels
- Growing global presence and diaspora reach across 65 countries, with distribution across television, Connected TV, OTT/IPTV and digital
- Highest-ever BARC performance with NDTV 24X7 securing multiple Top-2 rankings across several weeks
- Backing of the Adani Group / AMG Media Networks since the 2022 acquisition of a 64.71% majority stake, funding a transformation agenda across operations, technology and content
- Modernised technology backbone - 'Make in India' Production Asset Management (PAM) system using AI/ML, Adobe editing platform, VIZRT5 and WASP3D on-air graphics, and a new Newsroom Computer System
- Experienced and respected editorial team and a dynamic leadership team guiding strategic growth
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Data privacy and cyber security — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications. Data privacy risks encompass threats that can compromise the security and confidentiality of sensitive information, potentially leading to financial losses, reputational damage and legal repercussions, including data breaches, data discrimination and data brokerage. Cyber threats manifest as malware, phishing, ransomware and insider threats. Mitigations cited include a GlobalProtect firewall, Cisco Umbrella endpoint security, McAfee EDR with real-time threat detection, MFA-enabled VPN and Office 365 email, auto-patching, SAP for the finance system, regular security audits and employee training.
- Technology failure and platform availability — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: any technology failure can disrupt the business, with primary threats around software architecture, tooling, delivery and maintenance. Mitigations cited include cloud-hosted email on Microsoft with standard SLAs, scheduled Veeam backups to LTO tapes with a HOT DR disaster-recovery setup for on-premise servers, entirely in-house broadcast operations (studio, PCR and transmission), and hosting of both the content management system and user-facing websites on Amazon AWS to mitigate site non-availability.
- Compliance and governance / regulatory non-compliance — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: regulatory compliance and good corporate governance form the foundation of the Company, and non-compliance in any form can severely impact the business, brand name and credibility. Mitigated by a team of professionals reviewing applicable laws and regulatory changes and monitoring timely compliance through a compliance management tool, backed by an online statutory compliance management system with periodic Audit Committee and Board review.
- Employee health, safety and well-being — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk with negative financial implications: failure to ensure employee health, safety and well-being can impact overall productivity and consequently business operations, customer satisfaction and profitability. Mitigations include regular reviews by Internal Auditors, an on-premises creche staffed with a doctor and trained attendants, supervised shuttle services at early and late hours for women, two doctors monitoring sick employees with a daily report reviewed by management, sanitisation, regular fire-safety exercises and hazard/near-miss reporting.
- Cyber-attack exposure to the broadcast and IT environment — The Board's Report notes that in view of increased cyberattack scenarios, cyber security maturity is reviewed periodically and processes and technology controls are enhanced in line with threat scenarios, with real-time security monitoring across end-user machines, network, application and data layers. The Company states it did not face any incidents of data loss or data breaches in cyber security during the year under review - so the exposure is structural and managed rather than realised in FY26.
- Corporate restructuring / amalgamation of subsidiaries — The auditor's Emphasis of Matter draws attention to the Scheme of Amalgamation between the Company and its subsidiaries NDTV Networks Limited, NDTV Worldwide Limited, NDTV Media Limited and NDTV Labs Limited, effective 1 October 2025 and approved by the Regional Director (Northern Region), MCA Delhi. Comparative financial information has been restated to give effect to the amalgamation from the beginning of the previous year, so prior-period comparatives are not on the originally reported basis. The auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of this matter.

outlook.body:
- Digital-first transformation: adapt to changing consumption patterns by expanding presence across platforms, investing in technology that enables faster and more flexible content creation, and designing formats that match contemporary viewing habits
- Fortify foundations of long-term growth by deepening technological capabilities, expanding digital reach, enhancing production infrastructure, and integrating data-driven insights to sharpen efficiency and engagement
- Newsroom modernisation and integrated content infrastructure combining broadcast operations with advanced digital workflows, content management systems and production networks to deliver news across formats and geographies
- International expansion: broaden the global footprint across key markets, extend NDTV 24x7 distribution (e.g. Qatar), launch international OTT platforms in North America for diaspora audiences and scale NDTV World
- Adopt AI to improve newsroom efficiency and audience engagement while safeguarding editorial integrity, with verification, accountability and human editorial judgement remaining central
- Extend the brand beyond news through a new events vertical, 'NDTV Good Times', covering lifestyle, travel, food, culture and live entertainment, including concerts and large-scale public events
- Regional-language expansion of the broadcast network (NDTV Marathi, NDTV Rajasthan, NDTV MP-Chhattisgarh) alongside English, Hindi and business news brands
- Mid-term strategic priorities: expand reach among global Indian audiences and the diaspora, create a high-calibre talent pool, accelerate creation of new businesses and revenue streams, and maximise the ROI potential of all TV and digital content
- Strengthen the balance sheet and capital position, using the rights issue proceeds for debt repayment and for strategic initiatives across distribution, marketing and IP development
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: NDTV's expansion in FY 2025-26 is footprint- and platform-led rather than plant-led. Following the Adani Group's acquisition of a 64.71% majority stake in 2022, a transformation agenda was launched across operations, technology and content to strengthen distribution, modernise infrastructure and build a newsroom for the next era of media. Channel and platform build-out has proceeded in steps: NDTV Madhya Pradesh & Chhattisgarh, NDTV Rajasthan and NDTV World were launched in 2023 alongside a comprehensive brand refresh; NDTV Marathi was launched in 2024 together with expanded distribution across Connected TV, OTT/IPTV platforms and international markets, upgraded production and digital infrastructure, a strengthened presence across the UK, United States and MENA region, extension of NDTV 24x7 distribution into Qatar, and the launch of flagship intellectual properties including the NDTV World Summit. In 2025 the network launched a new events vertical under the 'NDTV Good Times' brand, extending NDTV into live cultural experiences, and initiated a 396.50 crore rights issue to strengthen the balance sheet and support strategic investments. During the year the Company added two dedicated mobile applications, NDTV and NDTV Profit, across iOS and Android, and strengthened its footprint across connected television, digital cable, IPTV and OTT environments. Its digital architecture runs on a hybrid cloud model - an on-premise in-house VM environment for control and flexibility, a private cloud for secure enterprise systems, and public cloud for collaboration and scalability - supporting remote production, faster publishing workflows and scalable infrastructure during peak news moments. For 2026 and onwards the Company states it will continue building NDTV into a global next-generation media network with accelerated investments across expansion of domestic and international distribution, brand building and audience engagement, development of new intellectual properties and content formats, and digital-first growth and partnerships with global platforms.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global media industry valued at approximately $2.58 trillion in 2025, with growth propelled by online video, mobile advertising and digital platforms
- India's Media and Entertainment sector reached 2.5 trillion in 2024 and is projected to expand to 3.07 trillion by 2027 (rupees)
- Digital media has already emerged as the largest segment of the Indian M&E sector, generating revenues of nearly 802 billion in 2024 (rupees)
- Television remains a formidable medium, particularly in news and current affairs, retaining its ability to shape national discourse and deliver credible information to diverse audiences
- Audiences now demand immediacy, accuracy and deeper context across multiple platforms; sustaining relevance requires blending editorial integrity with modern distribution capabilities
- Content discovery is shifting toward AI-led platforms and on-demand consumption; news is no longer consumed in a linear broadcast environment but through feeds, recommendations and on-demand formats across multiple screens
- Conflict and geopolitical turbulence generate intense demand for credible, verified reporting as audiences turn to trusted news organisations to distinguish fact from fabrication
- AI-driven content and disinformation pose serious challenges to trust, making verified journalism a differentiator for a credibility-led brand
- India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 estimated at 7.6% on robust domestic consumption, resilient services exports and a sustained investment cycle; Union Budget FY 2026-27 raised public capital expenditure to 12.2 lakh crore (rupees)
- IMF April 2026 World Economic Outlook projects global growth slowing to 3.1% in 2026 from 3.3% in 2025, with risks decidedly on the downside from conflict, geopolitical fragmentation and tariff regimes
- Balance-sheet lever: debt reduction from rights-issue proceeds lowered annual interest costs from over 21 crore to under 2 crore (rupees), enhancing financial flexibility
- Audience-share momentum cited as a growth driver: NDTV 24x7 recorded its highest-ever BARC viewership and became the No. 1 English news channel among affluent viewers; NDTV India achieved its highest-ever market share; NDTV Profit emerged as one of the fastest growing business news channels with market share exceeding 50% among key urban audiences
- The Company recorded revenues of 528.29 crore, 13.60% higher than the previous year, described by the CEO as reflecting steady operational progress as the platform scales (rupees)
